relevance_note: Case report of one man with a PSTPIP1 variant: 'The genetic analysis revealed a rare heterozygous variant [NM\_003978.4, c.764C>T, p.(Thr255Met), rs766895096] in PSTPIP1.'
method_note: Read by hand; no table. Two in-scope people: the case-report patient ('patient') and a previously published PAC syndrome patient cited as reference 5 ('ref 5 patient'), kept because the Discussion gives individual features (colitis, pyoderma gangrenosum, severe acne, no improvement with oral prednisolone). The Markdown escapes '>' as '>' and '_' as '\_'; spans keep the escaped text, while values for the HGVS and transcript fields are written with the plain characters (c.764C>T, NM_003978.4). rs766895096 is a dbSNP id, not coordinates, so genomic_coordinates is null. The ref 5 patient's variant is not printed (row kept with 'not reported'); the text says our patient's variant was 'a missense variant, similar to the variant reported in a previous patient', which I did not take as a stated variant type for ref 5. Age at onset left not reported: the first event (microscopic faecal blood at 60, with adenomas excised) may not be part of the disease; 67 years is the age at presentation, recorded as age at last evaluation. 'Computed tomography of the colon was normal' is a whole investigation; recorded as 'abnormal computed tomography of the colon' excluded, excluding nothing more specific. 'unlike our patient, the patient with PAC syndrome experienced severe acne' recorded as severe acne excluded for the patient; the broader checklist acne item is left not reported. Faecal calprotectin was elevated, but this is not serum MRP8/14, so the hypercalprotectinemia checklist item is not reported. Pyoderma gangrenosum histology was 'suggestive'/'compatible with, but not diagnostic of'; the abstract states it plainly, so it is observed. Lymphopenia arose on methotrexate. Figure 2 legend line contains a NUL byte; no span was taken across it. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: intravenous methylprednisolone for 5 days, then oral prednisolone tapered, with weekly subcutaneous methotrexate 25 mg (stopped due to lymphopenia); skin symptoms cleared after 7 weeks; prednisolone continued at 10 mg/day; currently methylprednisolone 5 mg/day and topical mesalamine
span: The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone 40 mg and 20 mg (morning and afternoon, respectively) for 5 days, followed by oral prednisolone, which was started at 40 mg and then tapered by 5 mg/week, with weekly subcutaneous injections of methotrexate 25 mg.
After 7 weeks of treatment, the skin symptoms cleared.
Prednisolone was continued at 10 mg/day, but methotrexate was stopped due to lymphopenia.
The patient is currently taking methylprednisolone 5 mg/day and using topical mesalamine.
